# Security policy

## Reporting a vulnerability

**Please do not open a public issue for a security problem.**

Use GitHub's private vulnerability reporting instead:
[Report a vulnerability](https://github.com/EFEELE/a11y-prefs/security/advisories/new).
It goes straight to the maintainers, stays private while it is being fixed, and gives
us a place to talk it through with you.

> If that link says the feature is not enabled, the repository owner has not switched
> it on yet. Say so in a normal issue — without any detail about the vulnerability
> itself — and it will be enabled.

## What is in scope

- The `a11y-prefs` npm package, everything under `src/`.
- The WordPress plugin, everything under `wordpress/`.

The plugin ends up installed on other people's sites, so anything affecting it jumps
the queue ahead of everything else in this project.

Things worth reporting even if they look small:

- Anything that lets one visitor's stored preferences influence another visitor.
- Any way to get markup or script through the settings screen into the front end.
  Every option is whitelisted or escaped in `A11y_Prefs_Options::sanitize()`; a way
  around that is a real finding.
- Any way to make the panel render outside its shadow root, or to reach the host
  page's DOM through it.

## What is not in scope

- Accessibility problems in the site the plugin is installed on. That is the theme's
  and the content's job, and this project says so on purpose.
- Vulnerabilities in WordPress core or in other plugins.
- Reports generated by a scanner with no evidence that the finding is reachable.

Accessibility bugs in the panel itself are very welcome, but they are not security
reports — use the accessibility issue template for those.

## What to expect

A first reply within a week. If the report holds up, a fix and a release, credit in
the advisory unless you would rather not be named, and a note in the changelog. If it
does not hold up you will get an explanation of why rather than silence.

This is a free project maintained in spare time. That is not an excuse for ignoring a
security report, but it is the honest reason a fix may take days rather than hours.

## Supported versions

The latest release only. There is no long-term support branch and there will not be
one while the project is at `0.x`.
